title: Level 1 (Beginner) - B-4
notes:
West leads the ♦J against 6♠. After East wins the first trick with the ♦A and continues the suit, South's only possible remaining loser is in the trump suit. South must avoid losing a trick to the ♠Q.

Cashing the ♠A and ♠K is better than taking the second round finesse ("8 ever, 9 never" is a bridge saying that means that when 8 cards missing the Queen are held one should finesse. When 9 cards are held, as in the spade suit, cashing the top honours is best).

The order in which the ♠A and ♠K are cashed is critical. If West has all 4 spades, nothing can be done. Even if the ♠A is cashed first, West can cover South's continuation of the ♠J or ♠10 with his ♠Q, making his ♠9 and ♠8 into a sure trick.

If East has all 4 spades, South can pick up the suit by cashing the ♠K first. He can subsequently finesse twice against East's ♠Q. This play is marked as West's spade void will show up when the ♠K is cashed. South can get to dummy in hearts to take a second finesse against East's ♠Q. Cashing the ♠K first is superior to cashing the ♠A as the former play picks up all 4 spades in East's hand.

If both defenders follow to the ♠K, South should play his ♠A on the second round ("9 never".
